body:
**Triage: escalated to the maintainer — `needs-user-decision` · `target:v17` · `Bug`. `domain:*` deliberately withheld; the ruling selects the lane.** Triage seat (whole-repo Routine), fire 08:47Z.

## Why this is not routable yet

The two options in "What a fix has to decide" do not land in the same package, so labelling a lane now would pre-empt the ruling:

| option | lands in | lane |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 — a system-context write resolves the install's organization the way a session write does | `packages/objectql` (engine write path) + `packages/core/src/security` (context resolution) | `domain:engine-core` |
| 2 — untenanted system writes stay, and the autonumber scope / `COALESCE(…, '__global__')` unique partition stops treating the pseudo-tenant as a peer | `packages/drivers/driver-sql` | `domain:drivers` |

This is the #8772 shape, and that precedent is why the label is withheld rather than guessed: that card was routed four ways across three lanes before its ruling, and the ruling *was* the lane selector. A pre-applied label would have been wrong. Same here.

## Premises re-verified on `origin/main` @ `6b6b606`, not inherited from the card

- `GLOBAL_TENANT` is live in `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` and `schema-drift.ts`, with `sql-driver-unique-tenancy.test.ts` pinning the partition behaviour — the `COALESCE` half of the card is real and tested-in.
- `fillAutoNumberFields` is in `driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` and `driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts` — **the counter side is duplicated across two drivers**, which the card does not say. Under option 2 the fix surface is two packages, not one. Worth knowing before the cost of the options is compared.
- The stamp itself is an injected field, not an explicit assignment: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:555` injects `organization_id` from `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` into every tenant-scoped object, and `engine.ts:8158` documents that the `beforeInsert` hooks are what stamp `owner_id` / `organization_id` / `created_by`. So option 1's edit site is the engine's stamp resolution, and the card's "read off the row, after stamping" description of `fillAutoNumberFields` is accurate — the defect is upstream of the counter, as the card says.
- Zero-hit discipline: no `stampOrganization` / `applyTenancy` / `resolveWriteOrganization` helper exists anywhere in `packages/` (counter-probe: `organization_id` itself returns many hits in the same roots, so the narrow zero is real). There is no single chokepoint to change — which is a cost input for option 1 and belongs in the ruling.

## `target:v17` — stamped, with the reasoning stated so it can be reversed cheaply

Two of the four release-blocker classes hold, and the first is the decisive one:

- ① **a defect on a released surface that users are hitting today** — measured on `17.0.0` GA in a live single-tenant install, minting duplicate values on fields the app declared `unique`, across at least five objects;
- ③ **existing-data / migration shape** — duplicates are already minted and, per the card, have propagated into notification bodies, approval trails and a cross-reference field, so renumbering is off the table at the reporting install.

⚠️ Honest caveat, carried in these briefs for thirteen fires: this seat has no ruling on whether a `target:v17` board means anything **after** GA, and has been leaving GA-surface cards un-nominated on that basis. I stamped this one anyway because it is the strongest class-① instance the board has seen — the defect is actively producing corrupt business identifiers on a customer install — and because over-marking for a day is the cheaper error. If the v17 board is closed at GA, drop the label in the same action that records that ruling.

## What the ruling has to cover, beyond picking 1 or 2

The card names a residual it says it cannot answer, and it is the part with a deadline: **already-minted duplicates on live installs.** The card's stated posture — report them, do not silently rewrite — matches the posture #8686's ruling took, but it is not yet ruled here, and every hour of runtime on an affected install adds rows. Please rule on it in the same pass rather than leaving it to the implementing card.

## Not a duplicate, and the neighbours are checked

- **#8686** — the seed-loader producer, closed COMPLETED by PR #8832. Confirmed closed. This card is the runtime producer; the backfill cannot reach it, and is self-undoing on any install with server-side automation.
- **#8672** — `pm:on-hold`, `domain:identity`, measured the same primitive (`{ isSystem: true }` insert ⇒ `organization_id` NULL) on `sys_permission_set`, where an org-less row is defensible. ⭐ **This card is the evidence that the on-hold reasoning does not generalise**, and #8672's restart condition should be read against it — on application objects the same primitive forks a declared `unique`. Whoever rules this should look at both together.
- **#8323** (tenant-scoped objects getting global unique indexes) and **#3696** (the original tenancy/uniqueness contradiction, closed against the multi-tenant reading) are the adjacent family; #3696 is worth re-reading because this reproduces on a **single**-tenant install in the *organization* dimension, which is not the axis it was closed on.

⛔ Not dispatched, per the standing rule that a `needs-user-decision` card is never dispatched. It is not `pm:blocked` either — nothing upstream is in flight; it is waiting on a person.

## Maintainer ruling — Option 1 (system-context writes resolve the install's organization)

Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat 2026-08-15 (session `session_01LXPH2ApQmyHYeZGHfYv7Xs`), verbatim 「接受你的所有建议。」, accepting the 18-card decision-box four-axis analysis presented in that session. This card's accepted recommendation: **Option 1** — a system-context write on a tenant-scoped object resolves the install's organization the way a session write does (the twin of #8686's ruling, one layer up). Recorded by the triage seat; `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same write, and **the ruling selects the lane** as the escalation comment anticipated: `domain:engine-core` (the engine's stamp resolution — `packages/objectql` registry injection + the `beforeInsert` stamping path).

Binding points:
1. **Single-tenant:** derivable ⇒ derive and stamp. The `__global__` fork must stop being minted by hooks/cron/system endpoints.
2. **Multi-tenant:** a system-context write must either carry an explicit organization or be **refused loudly** — ⛔ never silently default to `__global__`.
3. **Already-minted duplicates: report, do not rewrite** — same posture as #8686. The implementing dev files the duplicate-reporting deliverable as its own follow-up card (dedupe first) rather than folding renumbering into this fix.
4. Cost input from the escalation's verification, carried forward: there is **no existing chokepoint helper** — the edit site is the engine's stamp resolution, and `fillAutoNumberFields` is duplicated in `driver-sql` and `driver-turso` (relevant to tests, not to the fix site).
5. Cross-reference: #8672's on-hold reasoning ("org-less rows defensible for `sys_permission_set`") does **not** generalize to application objects — this ruling is the evidence; read both together when touching the primitive.

Model floor: this changes write-path behaviour and adds a refusal (accept-set change) ⇒ `claude-fable-5` mandatory; quota exemption (maintainer 2026-08-13) ⇒ `opus` only if fable is measured unavailable, recorded in the claim. `target:v17` stays — blocker classes ① and ③ per the escalation.

Three sibling dispatches are live in this lane's neighbour file `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (#8868+#8833, #8855, #8858) — **no overlap**: this card's surface is `objectql` + `core/security` and touches none of them.

## Tier — trying fable, not inheriting an hour-old reading

The ruling makes `claude-fable-5` a **mandatory floor** (write-path behaviour change plus a new loud refusal ⇒ accept-set change), with the maintainer's 2026-08-13 quota exemption as the only downgrade.

I measured fable exhausted at ~14:35Z today on #8676 and downgraded that card. ⛔ I am **not** carrying that reading forward — a quota reading decays, and treating a 60-minute-old measurement as current state is the exact substitution this lane has publicly corrected four times today. Dispatching at fable and re-measuring. If it walls again I will downgrade to `opus` and record the **fresh** measurement here, per the exemption's own wording (*"仅当 fable 实测不可用"*).

## Ruling implemented as written — ⛔ not re-adjudicated

Option 1 (`5302919977`), all five binding points carried into the dispatch verbatim, in particular:

- **Single-tenant:** derivable ⇒ derive and stamp; the `__global__` fork must stop being minted by hooks / cron / system endpoints.
- **Multi-tenant:** a system-context write must carry an explicit organization or be **refused loudly** — ⛔ never silently default to `__global__`. This refusal is the accept-set change that sets the tier.
- **Already-minted duplicates: report, do not rewrite** (the #8686 posture). The dev files the duplicate-reporting deliverable as **its own follow-up card, dedupe first** — ⛔ renumbering is not folded into this fix.

## Two stale-premise checks I ran before dispatching, rather than trusting the thread

- The escalation verified its premises on `origin/main` @ `6b6b606`; `main` is now **`8664a2c99`**. The dispatch tells the dev to re-verify the named sites on today's tree rather than transcribe those line references.
- ⚠️ The escalation's own `target:v17` caveat is still unresolved — that seat noted it has **no ruling on whether a `target:v17` board means anything after GA**, and stamped this one as the strongest class-① instance anyway. The ruling kept the label. I am not disturbing it, but flagging that the underlying question is still open and is a maintainer call, not mine.

**Tier downgrade recorded — `claude-fable-5` → `opus`, on a FRESH measurement.** Amends the `Container & model` line of my claim above.

I said in that claim I would not carry the hour-old fable reading forward, and I didn't. Dispatched at fable; it terminated on the wall:

> You've reached your Fable 5 limit.

That is a new measurement taken minutes ago, not the ~14:35Z one from #8676. Re-dispatched at `opus` under the maintainer's 2026-08-13 exemption (「fable 如果用完了,可以用 opus」). ⛔ No further downgrade — `opus` is the floor for this card.

The dispatch tells the dev explicitly that this card *wanted* the top tier and why (a live GA defect minting corrupt business identifiers, plus a new refusal on the write path), so the STOP conditions get slowed down on rather than worked around.

⚠️ For the maintainer, since this is now the **second** card today forced off its mandatory floor: fable quota has been exhausted since at least 14:35Z. The ruling floor exists because contract-shaped errors are the expensive ones, and the exemption is doing real work today rather than being a formality. If more accept-set cards land this session they will all take the same downgrade.
